case_number: Criminal Appeal No. 1307 of 2019 (Arising out of SLP (Crl.) No. 9431 of 2011)
summary: The appeal challenged the conviction and 20-year sentence of Ravinder Singh @ Kaku for the kidnapping and murder of two children. The High Court had upheld his conviction under Section 302 IPC based on circumstantial evidence, including motive (infatuation with the children's mother), partial last seen theory, arrest, recovery of material objects, and call records. The Supreme Court re-examined the circumstantial evidence and found the chain incomplete and not wholly inconsistent with innocence. It held that the prosecution failed to conclusively prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt, particularly regarding the last seen theory and motive. The conviction and sentence were set aside.
legal_provisions_cited: Hukam Singh v. State of Rajasthan
Eradu and Ors. v. State of Hyderabad
Bhagat Ram v. State of Punjab
C. Chenga Reddy and Ors. v. State of A.P.
final_judgment: The appeal was allowed. The conviction and sentence of the appellant, Ravinder Singh @ Kaku, were set aside, and he was acquitted.
